newsitem.title: UK: BP wins injunction against Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: BP wins injunction against Greenpeace.

text.p: British Petroleum won a court injunction on Tuesday banning the environmental group Greenpeace from disrupting the company's search for oil in the new Foinaven field in the North Atlantic.
The interim interdict was granted by Edinburgh's Court of Sessions following an eight-day protest by Greenpeace members who boarded the Stena Dee floating oil platform.
The platform was headed to the Foinaven field some 100 miles off the coast of Scotland.
The protest, which ended on Sunday, was aimed at halting oil exploration in the area.
The court order also applied to two Greenpeace employees, Sarah Burton and Chris Rose, and the master of its campaigning ship, Jon Castle.
BP has also launched a lawsuit against Greenpeace claiming 1.23 million pounds ($2.1 million) in damages for the disruption to its operations.
Greenpeace says the action could bankrupt its operations in Britain.
But a BP spokesman said: " We are not seeking punitive damages -- merely the money we have lost as a result of Greenpeace's illegal activities. We have no intention of bankrupting Greenpeace."

The Greenpeace campaigners' protest was aimed at halting oil exploration in the area but Greenpeace called off the occupation on Sunday saying it could no longer guarantee the safety of the protesters.
The four were each fined 200 pounds in a Scottish court on Monday after pleading guilty to breaching the peace.
Greenpeace appealed for public support in its court battle against BP.

"BP made 1.5 billion pounds profit in the first six months of the year -- it makes more in profit in 48 hours than Greenpeace receives in income in a year," Chris Rose, who is Greenpeace deputy executive director, said in a statement.

Greenpeace campaigners have also been blocking an Atlantic Richfield Co rig off the Alaskan coast to keep it away from a field in the Arctic Beaufort Sea. But a U.S. federal judge on Friday ordered the activists to stay outside a moving safety buffer around the mobile rig.
The blockades, aimed at fighting global warming, are part of Greenpeace's most ambitious campaign yet against the oil industry.
The group wants oil producers to switch to renewable resources, arguing that burning even existing reserves of fossil fuels will cause irreversible climate change.
